articles.headline: Harrison Jr. blocking out noise amid slow start for Cardinals
articles.description: Arizona Cardinals receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. hears and reads what's being said about him after his slow start to his third season, but he remains confident and still has the confidence of his teammates.
articles.body:
TEMPE, Ariz. -- Arizona Cardinals receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. hears and reads what's being said about him after his slow start to his third season, but he remains confident and still has the confidence of his teammates.

Harrison, who has one catch for 33 yards on four targets through two games this season, said Wednesday that he's not surprised by the reaction to his slow start, but said it hasn't been difficult to keep his confidence high. He didn't hesitate when asked where his confidence level is, saying he has "a lot of confidence in myself."

"Does your confidence come from results or does your confidence come from your process?" Harrison said. "And I think for me it comes from my process. So, my process isn't going to change whether I get zero catches or 10 catches. I'm going to still do the same thing week in and week out, Monday through Saturday to prepare myself for games. So I think that's where I have a lot of my confidence comes from.

"And obviously you want to have more of an impact in the game, but I think confidence really has to come from preparation more than anything."

Quarterback Jacoby Brissett said Wednesday that "nobody has lost confidence in Marv" despite his start to the season, while Harrison didn't shy away from the reality his season has gotten off to a slow and citing a number of reasons.

"It's definitely a combination of a lot of things," Harrison said. "For my route tree getting down the field, you need a lot of things to go right. You need the right coverage, you need protection to hold up, you need me to run a great route, you need obviously Jacoby to make the right pass and make the right read. So, I feel like it's never one person's fault for anybody's success or lack thereof, really.

"So, I think it's always a combination of a bunch of things and whether that's a lack of success or success in general."

Another reason, Harrison said, is because of the two defenses he's played this season. The Los Angeles Chargers gave him single coverage on just seven of 32 routes and the Seattle Seahawks are, simply, one of the best defenses in the NFL.

"Pretty much that simple," Harrison said. "Seattle's a really good defense and you don't want to give a lot of teams, especially a rival team, a lot of credit. But when you just look across the league, they're far beyond above everybody else, especially on the defensive side of the football. So, things like that happen."

Brissett said the two have had "good conversations" and has tried to lend an ear to Harrison whenever he needs it.

"It's easy to say, 'Oh, it's a long season' to other people, but to Marv it doesn't feel like it's a long season," Brissett said. "As a teammate and as a quarterback, you still have to be there for him because what if this week goes the same way? Am I just going to not be there? It's a new week and that's the benefit of it being so early in the season that you have multiple weeks to hopefully be out there and just be able to do better."

articles.headline: Ben Rice hits 40th and 41st homers as Yankees beat Rays 9-2 a day after Tampa Bay clinches AL East
articles.description: — Ben Rice hit his 40th and 41st home runs, Ryan McMahon added a grand slam while matching his career high with five RBI and the New York Yankees beat the Tampa Bay Rays 9-2 on Wednesday night.
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- — Ben Rice hit his 40th and 41st home runs, Ryan McMahon added a grand slam while matching his career high with five RBI and the New York Yankees beat the Tampa Bay Rays 9-2 on Wednesday night.


              Gerrit Cole (10-9) allowed two runs and three hits in 5 2/3 innings with eight strikeouts and three walks. The 2023 AL Cy Young Award winner had a 3.61 ERA and 131 strikeouts over 22 starts and 127 innings following his return in May from Tommy John surgery.


              A day after Tampa Bay clinched the AL East title, Rice hit the first pitch of the first inning from Mason Englert (0-4) into the right-field second deck for his fourth career leadoff homer and second this season.


              Rice added a solo drive in the fourth for his fifth career multihomer game and finished with three hits. He is tied for the AL home run lead with Baltimore's Pete Alonso, the Rays' Junior Caminero and Houston's Yordan Alvarez.


              George Lombard Jr. also homered for the Yankees and Cedric Mullins went deep for the Rays.


              New York is assured of hosting a best-of-three AL Wild Card Series starting Tuesday, likely against Boston. The winner will face the Rays in a best-of-five Division Series.


              McMahon had an RBI single in the second and boosted the lead to 7-0 in the third with his third career slam. 


              Englert, brought up to allow Rays starters extra rest ahead of the playoffs, allowed eight runs and nine hits in 4 2/3 innings.


              Rays manager Kevin Cash said left-hander Shane McClanahan won't recover in time for the Division Series but left-hander Garrett Cleavinger and right-hander Tyler Wells are possibilities. All three have forearm tightness.


              Up next
              Yankees RHP Cam Schlittler (14-6, 1.94 ERA) and Rays RHP Freddy Peralta (9-11, 4.56) start Thursday night's series finale.

articles.headline: Gray earns 18th victory, Monasterio drives in run, and Red Sox edge Guardians 1-0
articles.description: — Sonny Gray pitched six innings to tie Philadelphia’s Cristopher Sánchez for the major league lead with his 18th victory, Andruw Monasterio drove in the only run with a sixth-inning single, and the Boston Red Sox edged Cleveland 1-0 on Wednesday...
articles.body:
BOSTON -- — Sonny Gray pitched six innings to tie Philadelphia’s Cristopher Sánchez for the major league lead with his 18th victory, Andruw Monasterio drove in the only run with a sixth-inning single, and the Boston Red Sox edged Cleveland 1-0 on Wednesday night to snap the Guardians’ six-game winning streak.


              It was just the fifth win in 13 games for the Red Sox, who clinched a playoff spot on Sunday.


              The 36-year-old Gray (18-5) is in line to become the fourth Red Sox pitcher since 2000 to lead the AL in victories, joining Rick Porcello (2016), Josh Beckett (’07) and Curt Schilling (’04).


              Gray allowed four singles, struck out three, walked one and lowered his ERA to 2.72.


              Aroldis Chapman struck out the side in the ninth for his 35th save of the season.


              Cleveland starter Foster Griffin (15-6) gave up a run on 10 hits with seven strikeouts.


              The Guardians entered with a one-game lead over the White Sox atop the AL Central after winning the series opener Tuesday, but needed a win Wednesday combined with a loss by either the Rangers or Astros to clinch a postseason berth.


              The victory came with a price for the Red Sox when center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela left with right hamstring tightness after running out a single the same day he was activated from the injured list. He had been sidelined with a right a quad strain since Sept. 3 and made a diving headlong grab on Steven Kwan, the game’s first batter. 


              Jarren Duran singled leading off the sixth, advanced on a groundout and barely beat left fielder Kwan’s throw with a headfirst slide on Monasterio’s hit.


              Up next
              Red Sox LHP Ranger Suarez (8-4, 3.27 ERA) is slated to start the series finale Thursday. The Guardians had not named a starter.


              
                ------

Trending rumors

- Manchester United and Liverpool are interested in Crystal Palace defender Tyrick Mitchell, TEAMtalk reports. Mitchell entered the final 12 months of his contract in the summer, and it is said that Chelsea are also monitoring his situation, attracted to the opportunity of landing him on a free transfer.

- Bayern Munich have emerged as suitors for Manchester City striker Erling Haaland, according to TEAMtalk. The Bundesliga side are believed to see the 26-year-old as a potential future replacement for Harry Kane, who they want to remain at the Allianz Arena for a further two years before assessing whether a move for Haaland is possible. Meanwhile, TEAMtalk reports that Vincent Kompany's side are also keen on Nottingham Forest attacking midfielder Morgan Gibbs-White, and could be contenders for his signature next summer amid plans to add him to their squad with England compatriot Kane.

- Chelsea and Manchester City are exploring a move for AC Milan forward Francesco Camarda, according to TEAMtalk. The Blues are said to have tracked the 19-year-old for some time, and they are monitoring whether an opportunity to land him could arise due to a lack of minutes for the Rossoneri since returning from his loan spell at Lecce. Camarda scored one goal in 21 Serie A appearances last season.

- Napoli are struggling to make progress in talks with the representatives of midfielder Kevin De Bruyne over a new contract, transfer journalist Nicolo Schira reports. Discussions have reportedly stalled with the 35-year-old, who arrived at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on a two-year deal in the summer of 2025, and it is now said that they are "on the verge" of parting ways next summer. De Bruyne was previously linked with clubs in Major League Soccer and the Saudi Pro League before deciding to join Gli Azzurri.

The 22-year-old is believed to be on the radar of several clubs in Spain amid struggles to earn a place in Unai Emery's side, with 32 minutes of action in the Premier League spread across three substitute appearances. He is on loan from Chelsea, but any potential permanent move at Villa Park would require conditions to be met, which would see a £43 million proposed deal become official.

articles.headline: Matthew Liberatore pitches Cardinals to 5-1 victory that halts Pirates' 5-game winning streak
articles.description: — Matthew Liberatore ended an 11-start winless stretch and Alec Burleson got his major league-best 112th RBI as the St. Louis Cardinals defeated the Pittsburgh Pirates 5-1 on Wednesday night.
articles.body:
PITTSBURGH -- — Matthew Liberatore ended an 11-start winless stretch and Alec Burleson got his major league-best 112th RBI as the St. Louis Cardinals defeated the Pittsburgh Pirates 5-1 on Wednesday night.


              Liberatore (6-14) gave up one run and six hits in 5 2/3 innings with six strikeouts and no walks. His previous win came on July 11 against Atlanta in the left-hander’s last start before the All-Star break. Liberatore had lost eight straight decisions.


              Burleson singled in the first run in a three-run third that put the Cardinals ahead 3-1. Iván Herrera scored on a wild pitch and Leo Bernal hit an RBI single.


              Masyn Winn doubled home a run and scored on JJ Wetherholt’s single in the fourth to stretch the lead to 5-1. Wetherholt had three hits and José Fermín added two.


              The Pirates’ five-game winning streak ended. It matched their longest of the season.


              Brandon Lowe accounted for the Pirates’ lone run when he led off the second inning with his team-leading 34th homer, his first of two hits. Ryan O’Hearn had two doubles.


              Brandon Eisert (3-3) retired just two of the five betters he faced and was charged with three runs in relief of opener Lake Bachar.


              St. Louis (77-81) must win its final four games to avoid its first consecutive losing seasons since 1958 and '59. Pittsburgh (80-78) needs to at least split its last four games to finish with a winning record for the first time since 2018.


              Up next
              The rubber match of the three game-series is Thursday, with St. Louis RHP Kyle Leahy (10-5, 3.65 ERA) facing 2025 NL Cy Young Award winner Paul Skenes (10-11, 3.91).

articles.headline: Yelich, Turang homer as Brewers win 99th game of season, delay Phillies' possible playoff clinch
articles.description: — Christian Yelich and Brice Turang hit solo home runs, and the Milwaukee Brewers delayed Philadelphia’s potential postseason clinch with a 4-1 win over the Phillies on Wednesday night.
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- — Christian Yelich and Brice Turang hit solo home runs, and the Milwaukee Brewers delayed Philadelphia’s potential postseason clinch with a 4-1 win over the Phillies on Wednesday night.


              The Phillies needed both a win over the Brewers and a loss later Wednesday night by either Arizona or San Diego to secure their fifth straight trip to the National League playoffs. The Phillies started their run with a trip to the World Series in 2022, reached the NL Championship Series the next season and are coming off consecutive NL East titles.


              The Phillies have to settle for a wild-card berth this season and are likely to open the playoffs next week on the road. The Phillies, Chicago and San Diego hold the three NL wild cards headed into the final games of the season.


              The Phillies went 0 for 12 with runners in scoring position against the Brewers and left 10 runners on base.


              Phillies interim manager Don Mattingly said ahead of the game the team was willing to wait at Citizens Bank Park until after the Padres game ended, if necessary, to celebrate. No need to hang around.


              Aaron Nola (7-11) had turned around a miserable season and posted a 1.86 ERA over his last eight starts as the longest-tenured Phillie got the chance to clinch. With a playoff party looming, he instead surrendered Turang’s 20th homer of the season in the first inning and Yelich’s 12th of the year in the second.


              The Phillies scored their only run in the second inning after loading the bases with no outs against Brewers starter Logan Henderson (11-3). Henderson allowed four hits and one run over five innings to help the NL Central champion Brewers win their 99th game of the season.


              Trevor Megill worked a scoreless ninth for his 30th save.


              William Contreras extended his hitting streak to 11 games with a two-run single in the third for a 4-1 lead.


              Nola struck out eight in six innings.


              Up next
              The Brewers did not announce a starter for Thursday's game. The Phillies send RHP Andrew Painter (3-10, 5.59 ERA) to the mound.

articles.headline: Sources: Mavs' Dereck Lively II (foot) not cleared for camp
articles.description: Dereck Lively II's status for the start of the season has yet to be determined as he continues to recover from right foot surgery, sources said.
articles.body:
Dallas Mavericks center Dereck Lively II has not been cleared for training camp and his status for the start of the regular season has yet to be determined as he continues to recover from right foot surgery, sources told ESPN on Wednesday.

After playing a key role as a rookie in the Mavericks' run to the 2024 NBA Finals, Lively's promising career has been derailed by recurring problems with his right foot, which has been surgically repaired twice in the past 14 months.

Lively is ramping up toward being cleared for basketball activity, sources said, emphasizing that the team is not discouraged by his progress.

Dallas begins training camp Saturday.

Lively has played a total of only 43 games in the past two seasons. He underwent his second surgery in December, ending his 2025-26 season after appearing in only seven games.

Lively, 22, the No. 12 pick in the 2023 draft, is entering the final season of his rookie contract.

If healthy, the 7-foot-1, 230-pound Lively could be a significant part of Dallas' long-term core as the Mavericks attempt to build a contender around reigning Rookie of the Year Cooper Flagg.

Lively, an athletic big man who is an excellent finisher and versatile defender, has career averages of 8.4 points, 7.0 rebounds and 1.5 blocks in 22.9 minutes.

Dallas Mavericks center Dereck Lively II has not been cleared for training camp and his status for the start of the regular season has yet to be determined as he continues to recover from right foot surgery, sources told ESPN's Tim MacMahon.

After playing a key role as a rookie in the Mavericks' run to the 2024 NBA Finals, Lively's promising career has been derailed by recurring problems with his right foot, which has been surgically repaired twice in the last 14 months.

Lively is ramping up toward being cleared for basketball activity, sources said, emphasizing that the team is not discouraged by his progress. Dallas begins training camp on Saturday.

Extension unlikely as Knicks, Towns talks stall

Talks have stagnated between the New York Knicks and Karl-Anthony Towns on a contract extension, and an agreement is considered unlikely as the team begins training camp next week, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania and Vincent Goodwill on Wednesday.

The sides have spent extensive time discussing a potential extension during the offseason, but there has been no movement lately in negotiations, sources said, as the Knicks stand to go for a repeat following their first NBA title in 53 years.

The Atlanta Hawks are trading Dorian Finney-Smith to the Charlotte Hornets for Buddy Hield, Ryan Nembhard and cash, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

Leonard, Raptors agree to two-year extension

The Toronto Raptors and Kawhi Leonard have agreed to a two-year, $115 million extension, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Leonard now has a total of three years and $165 million left on his deal.

The 2026-27 season will be Leonard's first back in Toronto since the 2018-19 campaign, a season in which he helped lead the Raptors to their only title in franchise history.
